topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the scope of the course, student expectations, and the key learning outcomes for the lecture series.

topics.label: Genetic and developmental basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer develops through accumulated genetic and epigenetic alterations that disrupt normal differentiation programs and tissue architecture, highlighting the experimental models used to study them.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, progression, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the clinical and histological distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, the process of invasion and metastasis, and the standard nomenclature used to classify them.

topics.label: Mechanisms of mortality and tumor incidence across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors cause systemic illness and death, alongside the patterns of cancer incidence and mortality observed in humans and other animal species.

topics.label: Cancer screening and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the rationale, methods, histological basis, and limitations of clinical screening programs for detecting pre-cancerous and malignant lesions.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes and providing reminders for upcoming practical classes.
